orð ~ uerbum cognate, but audio is not cognate with heyra (*h2ḱh2ows-; Gk ἀκούω is, but Greek partners have λόγοι/ἔπος, not a *werdh- word); 'hear (the) words' is universal.

near_miss.lead: kýr ... til bana ~ gām haṃsi (*gʷʰen- + *gʷōws, killing cattle by malign agency)
near_miss.why_not: Both cognates present (bani < *gʷʰen-), but noun phrase 'til bana' vs finite verb; killing cattle is a natural topic; the saga context (mysterious cattle deaths) is only loosely like the AV anti-demon charm. Not distinctive enough.

near_miss.lead: frost + snow pair: reód ... sneachta ~ forst and sniw ~ nix ... pruina ~ sníor ... frost (*prews- + *sneygʷʰ-)
near_miss.why_not: Cognates in all four branches (Ir. reód, OE forst, Lat. pruina, ON frost; sneachta, sniw, nix, snjór), but frost and snow go together in any list of winter weather. The OE Azarias line translates the Latin Benedicite (pruina et nix), and the Irish is a late Early Modern poem. Natural co-occurrence, not phraseology.

near_miss.lead: nótt ok dag ~ νύκτες ἡμέραι (night-and-day merism)
near_miss.why_not: Only νύξ ~ nótt is cognate (ἡμέρα is not cognate with dagr); the merism is universal.
osna 'sigh' and prāṇa share *h2enh1- only at root level; spiorad is a Latin loan. Christian death scene; no collocation.

Verb and noun both cognate (ausa ~ ἀφύσσω, if that equation holds; vatn ~ ὕδωρ), but the pairing follows from what the verb means ('scoop liquid'). The ON is the name-giving rite of sprinkling a child with water (dative of instrument), the Greek is drawing water (accusative object): the contexts and syntax differ.

near_miss.lead: bleaghan na mbó ~ mjólka kýr (milk cows; *h2melǵ- + *gʷōws)
near_miss.why_not: Both pairs cognate (Ir. bligid/blegon ~ ON mjólk-; bó ~ kýr) and both scenes have a woman milking, but 'milk the cows' is fixed by the subject matter. Ved. uses duh- with gā́ḥ. Not distinctive.

near_miss.lead: father and mother (*ph2tḗr + *méh2tēr) pairings, kin lists
near_miss.why_not: Default kin terms in genealogy or lament lists; the pair is universal.
Calendar computation in Íslendingabók; numerals and time words only.

near_miss.lead: var hann þrjá vetr ok þrjú sumur ~ uvāsa bahulāḥ samāḥ (stay + accusative of duration; ON var/vas < *h2wes- 'dwell' ~ Skt vas-; sumar ~ samā < *sem-h2-)
near_miss.why_not: The best lead in the set: both lexemes are cognate, the syntax matches, and the context (a long sojourn) is similar. DCS has 'vas- + samāḥ' 13x in MBh (e.g. 'uvāsa ... trihimāḥ samāḥ', 'vasati śāśvatīḥ samāḥ'), plus BĀU and the Purāṇas. But in ON var is just the default past of vera; ON counts mainly in vetr, and 'var ... sumur' occurs only about 26x in Íslendinga sögur + Menota; the Skt witnesses are epic or later, with none in RV/AV. Verb + duration is universal syntax. Plausible but not defensible as an inherited formula.

near_miss.lead: edrych y goleu ... y lygat ~ darśata rocana (*derḱ- + *lewk-)
near_miss.why_not: Root-level co-occurrence only. Welsh: 'look at the light and open his eye' (Kei mocking the porter, Culhwch); the AV praises a shining chariot. No collocation.
ON fé means 'money' here (Oddr's fortune), Skt paśu 'livestock' sits in a 'sons, cattle, kin' list; no shared phrase.
Leaves of a book (Irish) vs leaves for baking (Cato); unrelated.
